newsitem.title: USA: Mass. housing agency needs to cut costs - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass. housing agency needs to cut costs - paper.

text.p: The Massachusetts Housing Finance Agency (MHFA) can avert a financial crisis and protect low-income housing sponsored by the agency, the Boston Globe said, citing a study due to be released Tuesday.

In its Tuesday edition, the paper said that the study would recommend the agency raise rents in 77 mixed-income developments, cut operating expenses at those projects, and recapitalize their ownerships with new investors.

The agency executive director, Steven Pierce, embraced the recommendations, as the best chance to steer the MHFA away from "the cliff" he said it otherwise would face in as few as five years, the Globe said.

At risk is $837 million in first mortgages issued in the 1980s under State Housing Assistance for Rental Production (SHARP) and a sister program. The loans account for 20 percent of the agency's $4.3 billion in assets.

Over the next 15 years, the MHFA faces a $255 million gap between the funds for the owners to repay the loans and debt service on the bonds issued to fund them. Already, 90 percent of the loans would be in default if the MHFA was not using about $5 million a year in reserves to plug the gap, Pierce told the paper.

The study, by real estate consultants, McCall & Almy, estimated an extra $170 million in operating income could be generated over 15 years by rasing rents on market-rate apartments and cutting operating costs.
